t: Ancient and modern figures for the Persian army are far apart: Herodotus gives 2.6 million military personnel, Ctesias 800,000, and modern scholars generally 120,000 to 300,000.
The Persians attacked the Greek position frontally on two days without success, and passed it only when a local man, Ephialtes, told Xerxes of the mountain path.
Thermopylae was a defeat for the Greeks in the war, but the stand of the rearguard became one of the most remembered episodes of the Greco-Persian Wars.
dyk: A hill on which the Greeks were thought to have died was identified differently after 1939, when the archaeologist Spyridon Marinatos found large numbers of Persian bronze arrowheads on Kolonos Hill.
ev: A Persian expedition destroys Eretria but is met at Marathon by a heavily outnumbered Athenian army, and the Persians withdraw to Asia
A congress at Corinth forms a confederate alliance of Greek city-states
The Greeks leave the Vale of Tempe and adopt Themistocles's plan to hold Thermopylae on land and the straits of Artemisium at sea
The Persian army is sighted across the Malian Gulf, and Leonidas refuses Xerxes's demand that the Greeks hand over their arms
Persian assaults on the first two days fail, and Ephialtes tells Xerxes of the mountain path
On the third day the Greek rearguard is surrounded and killed and the pass is opened
The Greek fleet defeats the Persian fleet at the Battle of Salamis
A Greek army defeats Mardonius at the Battle of Plataea, ending the invasion

f.date: 480 BCE, between July and September; the Persian army was sighted in mid-August, and the fighting lasted three days
f.place: The pass of Thermopylae, on the Malian Gulf, in central Greece; the pass is now several kilometres inland because of sedimentation
f.sides: An alliance of Greek city-states led by Sparta under King Leonidas I, about 7,000 men by the usual modern reckoning, of whom an estimated 300 were Spartans; the Achaemenid Persian Empire under Xerxes, with modern estimates of the whole army generally between 120,000 and 300,000, where Herodotus gives 2.6 million
f.outcome: The Persians forced the pass after a mountain path was revealed to them, and the Greek rearguard was killed, apart from the Thebans, most of whom reportedly surrendered. The Persians went on to overrun Boeotia and take Athens.
